title: Reinforcement Speculative Decoding for Fast Ranking

problem.claim: Autoregressive decoding creates latency challenges for LLM-based ranking systems.

gap.claim: Existing single-token and speculative-decoding approaches can degrade in tail positions or fail to satisfy ranking-specific latency and listwise-knowledge requirements.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Reinforcement Speculative Decoding for fast LLM ranking inference.
The method uses an up-to-down decoding paradigm in which an agent iteratively modifies the ranking sequence under a constrained budget.
The method combines ranking-tailored policy optimization with listwise ranking knowledge from items verified across rounds.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report theoretical robustness and advantages of their paradigm and implementation.
The authors report effectiveness on information-retrieval and recommender-system tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs are used in information-retrieval and recommender-system ranking.
Single-token decoding can suffer severe degradation in tail positions, while speculative decoding presents ranking-specific challenges.
The paper introduces reinforcement speculative decoding with constrained-budget, up-to-down sequence modification.
Ranking-tailored reinforcement learning optimizes multi-round modification and uses listwise knowledge from verified items.
The authors report theoretical advantages and effectiveness on IR and RS tasks.

unknowns: Exact latency budgets and verification-round limits are not reported.
Experimental datasets, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
The theoretical claims and implementation details are not specified.
